image.date_qualification: A photograph of the school at its North Brink site, taken c.2004; it depicts the school, not its 1379 foundation.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: CC BY-SA 3.0; UsageTerms: Creative Commons Attribution-Share Alike 3.0; Copyrighted: True

events.name: Foundation of Wisbech Grammar School

events.enhanced_description: In 1379, Timur launched a campaign against the Sufid Dynasty of Khwarazm, marking a significant expansion of his empire. This conquest solidified Timur's power in Central Asia and set the stage for further military campaigns.
events.name: Timur conquers the Sufid Dynasty of Khwarazm

events.enhanced_description: On May 29, 1379, John I succeeded his father, Henry II, as King of Castile and León, continuing the royal lineage during a period of political challenges in the Iberian Peninsula.
events.name: John I Succeeds Henry II as King of Castile and León

events.enhanced_description: On June 30, 1379, New College was founded in Oxford by William of Wykeham, Bishop of Winchester, contributing to the educational landscape of medieval England.

image.caption: Photograph of New College, Oxford.
image.credit: Simon Q from United Kingdom — New College, Oxford Uploaded by tm
image.date_qualification: A photograph of the college site, not a depiction of its 1379 foundation. Original image date: 2009-09-13 11:18.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: CC BY 2.0; UsageTerms: Creative Commons Attribution 2.0; Copyrighted: True

events.name: Foundation of New College, Oxford

events.enhanced_description: On July 1, 1379, forces from the Republic of Venice and the Ottoman Turks restored John V Palaiologos as Byzantine co-emperor in Constantinople, while his rival Andronikos IV was confined to Silivri.
events.name: Restoration of John V Palaiologos as Co-Emperor

events.enhanced_description: On September 9, 1379, the Treaty of Neuberg was signed, dividing the Austrian Habsburg lands between brothers Albert III and Leopold III, a significant event in the political landscape of the Habsburg dynasty.

locations.name: Neuberg an der Mürz, Styria, Austria

events.name: Treaty of Neuberg Signed

events.enhanced_description: In 1380, Sir William Walworth, a prominent member of the Fishmongers Guild, was elected Lord Mayor of London for the second time. His leadership was significant during a period of social unrest in the city.
events.name: Sir William Walworth becomes Lord Mayor of London

events.enhanced_description: In 1380, Khan Tokhtamysh of the White Horde successfully dethroned Mamai of the Blue Horde, leading to the unification of the two hordes into the Golden Horde. This event reshaped the political landscape of the region.
events.name: Khan Tokhtamysh dethrones Mamai

events.enhanced_description: In 1380, Karim Al-Makhdum arrived in Jolo, where he built a mosque, marking the introduction of Islam to the Sulu Archipelago. His efforts laid the foundation for the spread of Islam in the region.
events.name: Karim Al-Makhdum arrives in Jolo

events.enhanced_description: In 1380, the Hongwu Emperor of the Ming Dynasty purged his chancellor, Hu Weiyong, and abolished the chancellorship, consolidating power directly under the emperor. This marked a significant shift in governance in the Ming Empire.
events.name: Hongwu Emperor purges Hu Weiyong

events.enhanced_description: In 1380, the last islands of Polynesia were discovered and inhabited, marking a significant achievement in the exploration of the Pacific. This expansion contributed to the rich cultural tapestry of the Polynesian islands.
events.name: Last islands of Polynesia discovered

events.enhanced_description: In 1380, King Ferdinand I of Portugal founded the Companhia das Naus, a significant step in the development of Portuguese maritime exploration. This organization played a crucial role in the Age of Discovery.
events.name: Companhia das Naus founded

events.enhanced_description: In 1380, Paul Palaiologos Tagaris, appointed as the Latin Patriarch of Constantinople by Pope Urban VI, took residence in Chalcis. His appointment was controversial and reflected the tensions between the Latin and Orthodox churches.
events.name: Paul Palaiologos Tagaris takes residence in Chalcis

events.enhanced_description: In February 1380, Olaf II of Denmark was also crowned Olaf IV of Norway, with his mother Margrete serving as regent. This dual monarchy marked a significant moment in the unification of the Scandinavian kingdoms.
events.name: Olaf II of Denmark becomes Olaf IV of Norway

events.enhanced_description: On March 13, 1380, the southern English town of Winchelsea was attacked and burned by a French expeditionary force for the second time. This event was part of the ongoing conflicts during the Hundred Years' War.
events.name: Attack on Winchelsea

events.enhanced_description: On May 31, 1380, Grand Duke Jogaila of Lithuania signed the secret Treaty of Dovydiškės with the Teutonic Knights, which ignited a civil war against his uncle Kęstutis. This treaty had lasting implications for Lithuanian politics.

image.caption: Document of the Treaty of Dovydiškės between Jogaila and the Teutonic Order.
image.credit: Jogaila and the Teutonic Knights — Scan from A.Bumblauskas, Senosios Lietuvos istorija 1009-1795
image.date_qualification: Document of the treaty signed on31May1380, reproduced as a scan from a history book. The saved date identifies the treaty; an image creation or scanning date is not established.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: Public domain; UsageTerms: Public domain; Copyrighted: False

events.name: Treaty of Dovydiškės

events.enhanced_description: On June 21, 1380, the Venetian fleet achieved a decisive victory over the Genoese in the Battle of Chioggia. This battle was a pivotal moment in the War of Chioggia, significantly weakening Genoa's naval power.
events.name: Battle of Chioggia

events.enhanced_description: On July 27, 1380, Henry Bolingbroke married Mary de Bohun at Arundel Castle. This union was significant in the context of English nobility and would later play a role in the succession of the English throne.
events.name: Marriage of Henry Bolingbroke and Mary de Bohun

events.enhanced_description: On September 8, 1380, the Battle of Kulikovo took place, where Russian forces under Grand Prince Dmitry Donskoy successfully resisted a large invasion by the Blue Horde. This battle is often considered a turning point in the struggle against Mongol domination.

image.caption: Book illustration of Dmitry Donskoy learning Mamai’s plans from a captured Tatar.
image.credit: Book illustration — http://bibliotekar.ru/rus/98.htm
image.date_qualification: The illustration is dated to the 17th century; it does not depict the battle as a contemporary image.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: Public domain; UsageTerms: Public domain; Copyrighted: False

events.name: Battle of Kulikovo

events.enhanced_description: On September 16, 1380, Charles V of France passed away, and his twelve-year-old son, Charles VI, ascended to the throne. This transition marked the beginning of a tumultuous period in French history.
events.name: Charles VI of France succeeds Charles V

events.enhanced_description: On October 2, 1380, Caterina Visconti married her cousin Gian Galeazzo Visconti at the Church of San Giovanni in Conca. This marriage strengthened the Visconti family's political power in Milan.

locations.historical_name: Church of San Giovanni in Conca
locations.name: Church of San Giovanni in Conca

events.name: Marriage of Caterina Visconti and Gian Galeazzo Visconti

events.enhanced_description: On November 3, 1380, Charles VI of France was crowned at Reims Cathedral, following the death of his father, Charles V. His coronation marked the beginning of his reign during a challenging period for France.
events.name: Coronation of Charles VI of France

events.enhanced_description: In 1381, due to Joanna I of Naples' support for Antipope Clement VII, Pope Urban VI granted Naples to Charles of Durazzo. With Hungarian support, Charles advanced on Naples and captured Joanna, altering the power dynamics in the region.
events.name: Charles of Durazzo captures Joanna I of Naples

events.enhanced_description: In 1381, Venice emerged victorious in the War of Chioggia against Genoa after a series of naval battles. This victory significantly weakened Genoa's influence in the Mediterranean.
events.name: Venice wins War of Chioggia

events.enhanced_description: In 1381, Hajji I succeeded Alah-ad-Din Ali as Mamluk Sultan of Egypt, although the government remained under the control of the rebel leader Barquq. This transition reflected the ongoing power struggles within the Mamluk Sultanate.
events.name: Hajji I becomes Mamluk Sultan of Egypt

events.enhanced_description: In 1381, Timur launched a campaign against the Sarbadar dynasty, a local power in eastern Persia, effectively ending their rule and consolidating his control over the region. This conquest was part of Timur's larger ambition to establish a vast empire across Central Asia and the Middle East.

image.caption: Forensic facial reconstruction of Timur by Mikhail Gerasimov, shown in a modern photograph.
image.credit: user:shakko — Own work
image.date_qualification: A modern photograph of a forensic reconstruction, not a contemporary image of Timur or a depiction of the 1381 conquest. The source image date is 2008-08; the supported display date is 2008.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: CC BY-SA 3.0; UsageTerms: Creative Commons Attribution-Share Alike 3.0; Copyrighted: True

events.name: Timur conquers east Persia, ending the rule of the Sarbadar dynasty

events.enhanced_description: In 1381, Sonam Drakpa successfully deposed Drakpa Changchub, asserting his authority over Tibet. This political upheaval marked a significant shift in the leadership of the region during a time of considerable instability.
events.name: Sonam Drakpa deposes Drakpa Changchub as ruler of Tibet

events.enhanced_description: In 1381, the Ming dynasty annexed the territories of the former Kingdom of Dali, located in modern-day Yunnan and Guizhou provinces. This annexation facilitated the migration of hundreds of thousands of Chinese settlers, including military colonists, into the region, significantly altering its demographic landscape.
events.name: The Ming dynasty of China annexes the areas of the old Kingdom of Dali

events.enhanced_description: In 1381, during the reign of the Hongwu Emperor, the lijia census registration system was universally imposed across Ming China. This system aimed to improve tax collection and governance, revealing a significant population decline since the Song dynasty.
events.name: Lijia census registration system imposed in Ming dynasty China

events.enhanced_description: On March 14, 1381, Chioggia concluded an alliance with Zadar and Trogir against Venice. This alliance was part of the broader conflicts in the Adriatic region during this period.
events.name: Alliance of Chioggia with Zadar and Trogir

events.enhanced_description: On June 12, 1381, during the Peasants' Revolt, rebels from Kent and Essex, led by Wat Tyler and Jack Straw, gathered at Blackheath. They were encouraged by a sermon from the renegade priest John Ball, calling for social reforms.
events.name: Peasants' Revolt in England

events.enhanced_description: On June 14, 1381, during the Peasants' Revolt, rebels stormed John of Gaunt's Savoy Palace in London and attacked the Tower of London, executing Archbishop Simon Sudbury and Lord High Treasurer Robert Hales. This event highlighted the growing unrest among the peasantry.
events.name: Destruction of John of Gaunt's Savoy Palace

events.enhanced_description: On June 15, 1381, during negotiations of the Peasants' Revolt, Wat Tyler was murdered by the King's entourage. This assassination led to the collapse of the revolt as noble forces regained control over the situation.
events.name: Murder of Wat Tyler

events.enhanced_description: In August 1381, Kęstutis overthrew his nephew Jogaila as Grand Duke of Lithuania, allowing Jogaila to remain as governor of eastern Lithuania. This event marked the beginning of the Lithuanian Civil War.
events.name: Kęstutis overthrows Jogaila

events.enhanced_description: In 1382, Khan Tokhtamysh of the Golden Horde invaded Muscovy as retribution for Grand Prince Dmitry Donskoy's previous defiance against Khan Mamai. Despite the invasion, Dmitry was allowed to retain his position as ruler of Moscow after pledging loyalty to Tokhtamysh.

image.caption: G. Lissner’s retrospective illustration depicting the defense of Moscow against Tokhtamysh’s army.
image.credit: Г. Лисснер — Книга: «Русь и Кочевники» В. В. Каргалова , С. 355 (Собственный скан.)
image.date_qualification: The image is described as depicting the 1382 defense; the supplied image date, 2012-04-03, is not the depicted event date.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: Public domain; UsageTerms: Public domain; Copyrighted: False

events.name: Khan Tokhtamysh overruns Muscovy

events.enhanced_description: In 1382, the Ottoman Empire captured Sofia from Bulgarian control, further expanding their influence in the Balkans. This event was part of the Ottomans' broader campaign to dominate southeastern Europe.

image.caption: Banya Bashi Mosque in Sofia.
image.credit: xiquinhosilva from Cacau — 05158-Sofia
image.date_qualification: Photographed 2010-05-13; not contemporaneous with the 1382 event.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: CC BY 2.0; UsageTerms: Creative Commons Attribution 2.0; Copyrighted: True

events.name: Ottomans take Sofia from Bulgarians

events.enhanced_description: In 1382, Ibrahim I was selected to succeed Husheng as Shah of Shirvan, a region that is now part of modern Azerbaijan. His ascension marked a continuation of the local dynastic rule in the area.
events.name: Ibrahim I becomes Shah of Shirvan

events.enhanced_description: In 1382, Kęstutis, the Grand Duke of Lithuania, was captured by his former ally Jogaila during negotiations. This betrayal led to Kęstutis's murder and allowed Jogaila to reclaim control over Lithuania.
events.name: Kęstutis taken prisoner by Jogaila

events.enhanced_description: In 1382, Ahmed deposed his brother Hussain, taking control of the Jalayirid Dynasty in western Persia. This internal conflict highlighted the instability within the dynasty during this period.
events.name: Ahmed deposes Hussain in Jalayirid Dynasty

events.enhanced_description: In 1382, Rana Lakha succeeded Rana Kshetra Singh as the ruler of Mewar, a region in present-day Rajasthan, India. His reign would be marked by efforts to consolidate power and defend against external threats.
events.name: Rana Lakha succeeds Rana Kshetra Singh in Mewar

events.enhanced_description: In 1382, Conrad Zöllner von Rothenstein succeeded Winrich von Kniprode as the Grand Master of the Teutonic Knights. His leadership would influence the Order's military and political strategies in the Baltic region.
events.name: Conrad Zöllner von Rothenstein becomes Grand Master of the Teutonic Knights

events.enhanced_description: In 1382, Balša II of Zeta launched a military campaign to conquer Albania, expanding his influence in the region. This conquest was part of the broader conflicts in the Balkans during this period.
events.name: Balša II of Zeta conquers Albania

events.enhanced_description: In 1382, Dawit I succeeded his brother Newaya Maryam as Emperor of Ethiopia. His reign would be characterized by efforts to strengthen the empire and maintain its independence amidst regional pressures.
events.name: Dawit I succeeds Newaya Maryam as Emperor of Ethiopia

events.enhanced_description: In 1382, Abraham bar Garib was appointed as the Syriac Orthodox Patriarch of Mardin, a significant religious position within the Syriac Orthodox Church, which has deep historical roots in the region.
events.name: Abraham bar Garib becomes Syriac Orthodox Patriarch of Mardin

events.enhanced_description: On January 20, 1382, Princess Anne of Bohemia married King Richard II of England, becoming his queen consort. Although the marriage produced no heirs, it was significant in strengthening ties between England and Bohemia.

image.caption: 14th-century illustration of Anne of Bohemia in the Liber Regalis.
image.credit: Unknown English painter — http://www.history.ac.uk/richardII/images/liber2.jpg
image.date_qualification: The source dates the image to the 14th century; it does not establish that it depicts the marriage on 20 January 1382.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: Public domain; UsageTerms: Public domain; Copyrighted: False

events.name: Marriage of Princess Anne of Bohemia and King Richard II

events.enhanced_description: On May 12, 1382, Charles of Durazzo executed Joanna I of Naples, claiming the throne for himself and becoming Charles III of Naples. This act marked a brutal turn in the political landscape of Italy during the late 14th century.
events.name: Charles of Durazzo executes Joanna I of Naples

events.enhanced_description: On May 21, 1382, the Synod of London condemned the teachings of John Wycliffe, an early reformer whose ideas challenged the authority of the Church. This synod, disrupted by an earthquake, became known as the 'Earthquake Synod' and highlighted the growing tensions within the Church.
events.name: John Wycliffe's teachings condemned by the Synod of London

events.enhanced_description: In August 1382, the revered painting of the Black Madonna of Częstochowa was brought from Jerusalem to the Jasna Góra Monastery in Poland. This event marked a significant moment in Polish religious culture, as the painting became a symbol of national identity and devotion.
events.name: Black Madonna of Częstochowa brought to Poland

events.enhanced_description: In September 1382, following the death of her father Louis I, Mary was crowned as the King of Hungary. Her ascension was met with resistance, leading to political tensions as her sister Jadwiga was chosen to rule Poland instead.
events.name: Mary crowned King of Hungary

events.enhanced_description: On September 30, 1382, the inhabitants of Trieste donated their city to Duke Leopold III of Austria, seeking protection and stability under his rule. This act marked a significant shift in the political landscape of the region.
events.name: Trieste donated to Duke Leopold III of Austria

events.enhanced_description: In October 1382, James I ascended to the throne of Cyprus, succeeding his nephew Peter II. His reign would be marked by efforts to stabilize the kingdom amidst ongoing political challenges.
events.name: James I succeeds Peter II as King of Cyprus

events.enhanced_description: On October 20, 1382, Winchester College was founded in England, becoming one of the oldest continuously running schools in the country. This institution played a significant role in the education of the English elite.

image.caption: View of Winchester College and St Catherine's Hill from Winchester Cathedral tower.
image.credit: Hugh Chevallier — Geograph Britain and Ireland
image.date_qualification: Photograph taken in 2011; it depicts the college’s site, not its 1382 founding.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: CC BY-SA 2.0; UsageTerms: Creative Commons Attribution-Share Alike 2.0; Copyrighted: True

events.name: Winchester College founded

events.enhanced_description: The Division of Chemnitz in 1382 marked the fragmentation of the territory governed by the House of Wettin into five parts, leading to significant political changes in the region. This division had lasting implications for the governance and territorial organization in Saxony.
events.name: Division of Chemnitz

events.enhanced_description: On November 27, 1382, the Battle of Roosebeke took place, where a French army led by Louis II, Count of Flanders, defeated the Flemish forces commanded by Philip van Artevelde. This battle was pivotal in the struggle for control over Flanders during the Hundred Years' War.

image.caption: Illuminated manuscript illustration of the Battle of Westrozebeke by Loyset Liédet.
image.credit: Loyset Liédet — http://www.waterwijk.be/content/images/A4A98230-23D0-4940-96C6-27B0F41B5098.jpg
image.date_qualification: Retrospective illustration in the Chronicle of Jean Froissart; described as dating to 1405. The supplied image date, 2007-05-15, is not the depiction date.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: Public domain; UsageTerms: Public domain; Copyrighted: False

events.name: Battle of Roosebeke

events.enhanced_description: On November 27, 1382, Barquq successfully deposed Hajji II, marking the end of the Bahri and Qalawunid Dynasties and the beginning of the Burji Dynasty in Egypt. This transition was significant in the power dynamics of the Mamluk Sultanate.
events.name: Barquq deposes Hajji II as Mamluk Sultan of Egypt

events.enhanced_description: In 1383, Charles III of Naples assumed control over Achaea, a region in southern Greece, furthering the influence of the Kingdom of Naples in the Mediterranean.
events.name: Charles III of Naples becomes ruler of Achaea

events.enhanced_description: Otto, Duke of Brunswick-Grubenhagen, became the ruler of Taranto in 1383, following the death of his wife, Joanna I of Naples, thereby continuing the dynastic connections in southern Italy.
events.name: Otto becomes ruler of Taranto

events.enhanced_description: In 1383, Louis I, Duke of Anjou, inherited the claim to the Latin Empire, a title he never formally used, reflecting the complex political landscape of post-Crusade Europe.
events.name: Louis I inherits claim to the Latin Empire

events.enhanced_description: In 1383, the Teutonic Knights resumed their military campaigns against pagan Lithuania, continuing their efforts to expand Christian influence in the region.
events.name: Teutonic Knights recommence war against Lithuania

events.enhanced_description: Dan I succeeded his father Radu as Prince of Wallachia in 1383, marking the continuation of the Dănești dynasty in the region.
events.name: Dan I succeeds as Prince of Wallachia

events.enhanced_description: In 1383, Rao Chanda succeeded Rao Biram Dev as the Rathore ruler of Marwar in western India, continuing the lineage of the Rathore dynasty.
events.name: Rao Chanda succeeds as Rathore ruler of Marwar

events.enhanced_description: In 1383, Löwenbräu beer was first brewed in Munich, Bavaria, establishing a brewing tradition that would become renowned worldwide.
events.name: Löwenbräu beer is first brewed

events.enhanced_description: The original inner courtyard of Farleigh Hungerford Castle in Somerset, England, was completed in 1383, showcasing the architectural style of the period.
events.name: Completion of Farleigh Hungerford Castle

events.enhanced_description: In 1383, the Wat Phra That Doi Suthep Temple was constructed in Chiang Mai, Thailand, under the reign of King Kuena of Lanna, becoming a significant religious site.
events.name: Wat Phra That Doi Suthep Temple is built

events.enhanced_description: The construction of the Bastille fortress in Paris was completed in 1383, which would later become a symbol of royal authority and a focal point during the French Revolution.

image.caption: Anonymous drawing of the Bastille’s eastern façade.
image.credit: Anonymous Unknown author — This file comes from Gallica Digital Library and is available under the digital ID btv1b103025059
image.date_qualification: The depicted date is 1790 or 1791, centuries after the event dated 1383; the source gives the image date as 1790.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: Public domain; UsageTerms: Public domain; Copyrighted: False

events.name: Construction of the Bastille fortress is completed

events.enhanced_description: On May 17, 1383, King John I of Castile and León married Beatrice of Portugal, a union that aimed to strengthen ties between the two kingdoms and had significant implications for the political landscape of the Iberian Peninsula.
events.name: King John I of Castile and Leon marries Beatrice of Portugal

events.enhanced_description: James of Baux, the last titular Latin Emperor and ruler of Taranto and Achaea, died on July 7, 1383, without an heir, leading to a power vacuum and changes in the political dynamics of the region.
events.name: James of Baux dies childless

events.enhanced_description: On October 22, 1383, King Fernando I of Portugal died, leading to the ascension of his daughter Beatrice and triggering the 1383–85 Crisis, a period marked by civil strife and conflict over the Portuguese crown.
events.name: King Fernando I of Portugal dies

events.enhanced_description: From May to September 1384, the Castilian army laid siege to Lisbon during the 1383–85 Crisis in Portugal, a pivotal conflict that would shape the future of the Portuguese monarchy.
events.name: Siege of Lisbon by the Castilian army

events.enhanced_description: In 1384, the Hongwu Emperor reinstated the Imperial examination system for civil service recruitment, reversing a previous suspension and emphasizing meritocracy in governance.
events.name: Hongwu Emperor reinstates Imperial examination system

events.enhanced_description: In 1384, the Nasrid princes of Al-Andalus replaced Abu al-Abbas with Abu Faris Musa ibn Faris as the ruler of the Marinid dynasty in Morocco, reflecting the shifting power dynamics in North Africa.
events.name: Nasrid princes replace ruler of Marinid dynasty

events.enhanced_description: In 1384, Zain Al-Abidin succeeded his father, Shah Shuja, as the ruler of the Muzaffarids in central Persia, continuing the legacy of his dynasty.
events.name: Zain Al-Abidin succeeds as ruler of Muzaffarids

events.enhanced_description: Shortly before his death in 1384, John Wycliffe sent out tracts criticizing Pope Urban VI, expressing his disillusionment with the papacy and advocating for reform within the Church.
events.name: John Wycliffe sends out tracts against Pope Urban VI

events.enhanced_description: In 1384, Qara Muhammad succeeded Bairam Khawaja as the ruler of the Kara Koyunlu, a Turkoman dynasty that controlled parts of Armenia and northern Iraq.
events.name: Qara Muhammad succeeds as ruler of Kara Koyunlu

events.enhanced_description: In 1384, Timur launched a campaign that resulted in the conquest of the northern territories of the Jalayirid Empire in western Persia, expanding his influence in the region.
events.name: Timur conquers northern territories of Jalayirid Empire

events.enhanced_description: In 1384, Katharine Lady Berkeley's School was founded in Gloucestershire, England, contributing to the educational landscape of the region.
events.name: Katharine Lady Berkeley's School is founded

events.enhanced_description: On August 16, 1384, the Hongwu Emperor of Ming China heard a case involving a couple who tore paper money notes, ultimately deciding to pardon them, highlighting the emperor's approach to justice.
events.name: Hongwu Emperor hears case of torn paper money

events.enhanced_description: On November 16, 1384, ten-year-old Jadwiga was crowned "King" of Poland in Kraków, marking a significant moment in Polish history as she became a female monarch in a male-dominated society.
events.name: Jadwiga crowned "King" of Poland

events.enhanced_description: On December 25, 1384, the use of the Spanish era dating system was suppressed in the Crown of Castile, reflecting changes in administrative practices and the influence of the Catholic Church.
events.name: Suppression of Spanish era dating system

events.enhanced_description: The Union of Krewo, established in 1385, marked the beginning of the Jagiellonian dynasty in Poland and Lithuania through the proposed marriage of Queen Jadwiga of Poland and Grand Duke Jogaila of Lithuania. This union also facilitated the acceptance of Roman Catholicism by the Lithuanian elite.
events.name: Union of Krewo

events.enhanced_description: In 1385, Tokhtamysh of the Golden Horde conquered parts of the Jalayirid Sultanate in western Persia, leading to a significant rift with Timur of the Timurid Empire, who also sought to expand into Persia. This conflict highlighted the power struggles in the region during this period.
events.name: Tokhtamysh Conquers Jalayirid Sultanate

events.enhanced_description: In 1385, Olav IV of Norway was elected as the titular King of Sweden, opposing the unpopular King Albert. This election reflected the ongoing political tensions in the Nordic region during this period.
events.name: Election of Olav IV of Norway as King of Sweden

events.enhanced_description: In 1385, after a series of tribute missions, the Hongwu Emperor of China's Ming dynasty agreed to invest King U of Goryeo, solidifying the relationship between the two states. This event marked a significant diplomatic achievement for Goryeo.
events.name: Hongwu Emperor Invests King U of Goryeo

events.enhanced_description: In 1385, significant architectural projects were undertaken, including the construction of Castello Estense in Ferrara, Italy, and Bodiam Castle in East Sussex, England. These castles exemplified the military and residential architecture of the period.
events.name: Construction of Castello Estense and Bodiam Castle

events.enhanced_description: On July 17, 1385, Charles VI of France married Isabeau of Bavaria in a politically motivated union aimed at strengthening ties between France and Bavaria. The wedding was celebrated with France's first court ball, marking a significant cultural event in the royal court.
events.name: Marriage of Charles VI of France and Isabeau of Bavaria

events.enhanced_description: On August 6, 1385, Edmund of Langley was elevated to the title of Duke of York, becoming the first to hold this title. This elevation marked a significant moment in the English nobility and the political landscape of the time.
events.name: Elevation of Edmund of Langley to Duke of York

events.enhanced_description: On August 14, 1385, the Battle of Aljubarrota took place, where John of Aviz decisively defeated John I of Castile. This battle was crucial in the 1383–85 Crisis in Portugal, leading to John of Aviz being crowned King John I of Portugal and securing Portuguese independence from Castile.
events.name: Battle of Aljubarrota

events.enhanced_description: On August 31, 1385, King Richard II of England initiated an invasion of Scotland, during which English forces burned Holyrood and parts of Edinburgh. However, the campaign ended without a decisive battle, highlighting the ongoing tensions between England and Scotland.
events.name: Richard II's Invasion of Scotland

events.enhanced_description: On September 18, 1385, the Battle of Savra occurred near Berat, where Serbian forces led by Balša II and Ivaniš Mrnjavčević faced defeat against the Ottoman commander Hayreddin Pasha. This battle was part of the larger conflict between the Serbian and Ottoman empires.
events.name: Battle of Savra

events.enhanced_description: On October 15, 1385, the Battle of Valverde took place, where the armies of Portugal achieved a significant victory over Castile. This battle was part of the ongoing conflict between the two kingdoms during the 1383–85 Crisis.
events.name: Battle of Valverde

events.enhanced_description: In December 1385, a group of Hungarian nobles assisted Charles III of Naples in overthrowing Queen Mary, who ruled over Hungary and Croatia. This political maneuver significantly altered the power dynamics in the region.
events.name: Hungarian Nobles Support Charles III of Naples

events.enhanced_description: In 1386, Queen Mary of Hungary was reinstated as the ruler of Hungary and Croatia after a period of political turmoil. Her return to power was significant in stabilizing the region during a time of conflict.
events.name: Reinstatement of Queen Mary of Hungary

events.enhanced_description: In 1386, Ladislaus of Anjou ascended to the throne of Naples, following the legacy of his father, Charles III. His reign marked a significant period in the political landscape of Southern Italy, characterized by conflicts with rival factions and the ongoing struggle for power in the region.
events.name: Charles' son, Ladislaus, becomes King of Naples

events.enhanced_description: The year 1386 marked the beginning of an interregnum in Achaea, a region in the Peloponnese, which lasted until 1396. During this tumultuous period, various pretenders vied for control, but none were able to establish a stable reign, leading to political instability.
events.name: A period of interregnum begins in Achaea, lasting until 1396

events.enhanced_description: In 1386, the mother and sister of Queen Jadwiga of Poland were kidnapped by rebels in the region that is now Hungary and Croatia. This incident highlighted the political turmoil and instability in the region during this period, affecting the royal family of Poland.
events.name: The mother and sister of Queen Jadwiga of Poland are kidnapped by rebels in Hungary-Croatia

events.enhanced_description: In 1386, Abu al-Abbas was reinstated as the ruler of the Marinid dynasty in Morocco. His return to power was significant for the stability of the Marinid Sultanate, which had faced internal strife and external threats during this period.
events.name: Abu al-Abbas is reinstated as ruler of the Marinid dynasty in modern-day Morocco

events.enhanced_description: In 1386, the Republic of Venice successfully took control of the island of Corfu, solidifying its influence in the Adriatic Sea. This acquisition was part of Venice's broader strategy to expand its maritime empire and secure trade routes.
events.name: The Republic of Venice takes control of the island of Corfu

events.enhanced_description: The construction of the Brancacci Chapel in Florence began in 1386, marking a significant moment in Renaissance art and architecture. The chapel would later become renowned for its frescoes by Masaccio and Masolino, which are considered masterpieces of early Renaissance art.
events.name: Construction begins on the Brancacci Chapel in Florence

events.enhanced_description: In 1386, the Rozhdestvensky Monastery was established in Muscovy, contributing to the religious and cultural landscape of the region. This monastery would play a significant role in the spiritual life of the community in the years to come.
events.name: Rozhdestvensky monastery is built in Muscovy

events.enhanced_description: On February 24, 1386, Elizabeth of Bosnia orchestrated the assassination of Charles III of Naples, who ruled over Hungary, Naples, Achaea, and Croatia. This act was a pivotal moment in the political turmoil of the region.
events.name: Assassination of Charles III of Naples

events.enhanced_description: On March 4, 1386, Grand Duke Jogaila, after being baptized and marrying Queen Jadwiga, was crowned Władysław II Jagiełło, King of Poland. This event marked the beginning of the Jagiellonian dynasty and a significant shift in Polish history.
events.name: Coronation of Władysław II Jagiełło

events.enhanced_description: On May 9, 1386, King John I of Portugal and King Richard II of England ratified the Treaty of Windsor, which established a strong alliance between the two kingdoms. This treaty was significant in shaping the political landscape of the late 14th century.
events.name: Ratification of the Treaty of Windsor

events.enhanced_description: On May 20, 1386, the city of Pitești in modern-day Romania was first recorded in historical documents. This mention marks an important point in the city's history and development.
events.name: Earliest Mention of Pitești

events.enhanced_description: In July 1386, John of Gaunt left England to pursue his claim to the throne of Castile, based on his marriage to Constanza of Castile in 1371. This expedition was part of the broader conflicts involving English and Spanish nobility.
events.name: John of Gaunt's Claim to Castile

events.enhanced_description: On July 9, 1386, the Battle of Sempach was fought, where Swiss forces secured their independence from Habsburg rule. This battle was a pivotal moment in Swiss history, reinforcing their autonomy.
events.name: Battle of Sempach

events.enhanced_description: On September 23, 1386, Dan I of Wallachia was killed in battle against the Bulgarians, leading to the ascension of Mircea the Elder, who would become one of the most significant rulers of Wallachia. This transition marked a crucial moment in the region's history.
events.name: Death of Dan I of Wallachia

events.enhanced_description: On October 18, 1386, Heidelberg University was founded by Rupert I, Elector Palatine, making it the oldest university in Germany. This institution became a significant center of learning and scholarship in Europe.
events.name: Founding of Heidelberg University

events.enhanced_description: On November 21, 1386, Timur, the leader of the Timurid dynasty, captured and sacked the Georgian capital of Tbilisi, taking King Bagrat V prisoner. This invasion marked a significant event in the history of Georgia and the expansion of Timur's empire.
events.name: Timur's Invasion of Georgia

events.enhanced_description: In 1387, Elizabeta Kotromanic, the mother of Mary, Queen of Hungary, was murdered in prison by Croatian rebels. This act of violence underscored the political instability and conflict in the region, as her daughter was later liberated.
events.name: Elizabeta Kotromanic is murdered in prison by Croatian rebels

events.enhanced_description: In 1387, Charles III ascended to the throne of Navarre following the death of his father, Charles II. His reign would be marked by efforts to strengthen the kingdom and navigate the complex political landscape of the Iberian Peninsula.
events.name: Charles III ascends to the throne of Navarre

events.enhanced_description: In 1387, Timur launched a campaign that resulted in the conquest of the Muzaffarid Empire in central Persia. Following his victory, he appointed three puppet rulers to maintain control over the region, further expanding his influence.
events.name: Timur conquers the Muzaffarid Empire

events.enhanced_description: In 1387, Khan Tokhtamysh of the Golden Horde invaded the Timurid Empire but was forced to withdraw due to heavy snowfall. This invasion highlighted the ongoing conflicts between the Golden Horde and the Timurid Empire during this period.
events.name: Khan Tokhtamysh invades the Timurid Empire

events.enhanced_description: In 1387, Maghan II succeeded his brother, Musa II, as Mansa of the Mali Empire. His ascension marked a continuation of the legacy of one of the wealthiest empires in West Africa, known for its trade and cultural achievements.
events.name: Maghan II succeeds Musa II as Mansa of the Mali Empire

events.enhanced_description: On January 5, 1387, John I succeeded his father, Peter IV, as King of Aragon and Valencia. His reign was characterized by alliances with France and Castile, which would shape the political dynamics of the region.
events.name: John I succeeds his father, Peter IV, as King of Aragon and Valencia

events.enhanced_description: On March 11, 1387, the Battle of Castagnaro took place, where forces from Padua, led by the English mercenary John Hawkwood, achieved victory over Giovanni Ordelaffi of Verona. This battle was significant in the context of the ongoing conflicts in Northern Italy during this period.
events.name: Battle of Castagnaro

events.enhanced_description: On March 24, 1387, the Battle of Margate occurred off the coast of Margate, where the Kingdom of England achieved a decisive victory over a Franco-Castilian-Flemish fleet. This battle was part of the larger conflict between England and France during the Hundred Years' War.
events.name: Battle of Margate

events.enhanced_description: On June 2, 1387, John Holland, a maternal half-brother of Richard II of England, was created Earl of Huntingdon. This title was significant in the context of the political alliances and power struggles of the English nobility during Richard II's reign.
events.name: John Holland created Earl of Huntingdon

events.enhanced_description: On August 22, 1387, Olaf, the King of Norway and Denmark, died, leaving a power vacuum in the kingdoms he ruled. His death led to the regency of his mother, Margaret I of Denmark, who would soon become a powerful queen in her own right.
events.name: Death of Olaf, King of Norway and Denmark

events.enhanced_description: On September 27, 1387, Petru of Moldavia paid homage to Władysław II Jagiełło, effectively making Moldavia a Polish fief. This act solidified Polish influence in the region, which would last until 1497.
events.name: Petru of Moldavia pays homage to Władysław II Jagiełło

events.enhanced_description: On December 19, 1387, the Battle of Radcot Bridge took place, where forces loyal to Richard II were defeated by rebellious barons known as the Lords Appellant. This defeat led to Richard II's imprisonment and significant changes in the governance of England.
events.name: Battle of Radcot Bridge

events.enhanced_description: In February 1388, the Merciless Parliament convened in London and convicted the entire court of Richard II of treason, leading to executions and exiles. This event marked a significant shift in power dynamics, effectively reducing Richard II to a puppet of the Lords Appellant.

image.caption: Retrospective illustration depicting the Lords Appellant demanding that Richard II let them prove their rebellion by arms.
image.credit: James William Edmund Doyle / Edmund Evans — Doyle, James William Edmund (1864) " Richard II " in A Chronicle of England: B.C. 55 – A.D. 1485 , London : Longman, Green, Longman, Roberts & Green, pp. p. 328 Retrieved on 12 November 2010.
image.date_qualification: The illustration is dated 1864, nearly five centuries after the 1388 parliamentary session.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: Public domain; UsageTerms: Public domain; Copyrighted: False

events.name: The Merciless Parliament convicts Richard II's court of treason

events.enhanced_description: In 1388, Mircea I of Wallachia successfully asserted control over the Dobruja region, thwarting Ottoman ambitions in the area. This strategic move was crucial in maintaining Wallachian independence during a period of increasing Ottoman expansion in the Balkans.
events.name: Mircea I of Wallachia takes control of the region of Dobruja

events.enhanced_description: In 1388, Petru of Moldavia received the region of Pokuttya as a pawn for a loan from the Polish king, highlighting the intricate political alliances and dependencies in Eastern Europe during this period. This arrangement underscored the financial and military pressures faced by Moldavia.
events.name: Petru of Moldavia receives Pokuttya

events.enhanced_description: In 1388, John Purvey completed the revision of Wycliffe's Bible, which played a significant role in the early English Reformation. This revision was pivotal in promoting the translation of the scriptures into the vernacular, leading to increased scrutiny of the Church's practices.
events.name: The revision of Wycliffe's Bible

events.enhanced_description: In 1388, John of Gaunt, uncle to Richard II of England, negotiated a peace with Castile, relinquishing his claim to the throne in favor of a marriage alliance between his daughter Catherine and Prince Henry of Castile. This diplomatic maneuver aimed to strengthen ties between England and Spain.

image.caption: Manuscript illustration of John of Gaunt and Blanche of Lancaster.
image.credit: Unknown author Unknown author — https://www.bl.uk/manuscripts/FullDisplay.aspx?ref=Harley_MS_7353
image.date_qualification: Image date: between circa 1461 and circa 1470; this is the manuscript’s date, not the date of the 1388 event.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: CC BY-SA 4.0; UsageTerms: Creative Commons Attribution-Share Alike 4.0; Copyrighted: True

events.name: John of Gaunt makes peace with Castile

events.enhanced_description: In 1388, the title of Prince of Asturias was established, marking a significant development in the Spanish monarchy's hierarchy. This title would later become associated with the heir apparent to the Spanish throne, symbolizing the importance of Asturias in the royal lineage.

image.caption: Portrait of Philip of Spain, Prince of Asturias, by Bartolomé González y Serrano.
image.credit: Bartolomé González y Serrano — Extracted from File:Bartolomé González y Serrano 003.jpg
image.date_qualification: Circa 1612; this is a later portrait, not an image of the title’s creation in 1388.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: Public domain; UsageTerms: Public domain; Copyrighted: False

events.name: The title of Prince of Asturias is created

events.enhanced_description: In 1388, Ramesuan was reinstated as the King of Ayutthaya after a violent coup that saw the execution of the young King Thong Lan. This event marked a turbulent period in the history of the Ayutthaya Kingdom, characterized by power struggles and political instability.
events.name: Ramesuan is reinstated as King of Ayutthaya

events.enhanced_description: In 1388, General Yi Seong-gye initiated a revolution against the Goryeo dynasty after being ordered to confront a superior Chinese army. This uprising ultimately led to the downfall of King U and the ascension of his son, King Chang, marking a significant shift in Korean history.
events.name: Goryeo Revolution begins

events.enhanced_description: In 1388, Tran Ngung successfully overthrew Tran Hien, marking a significant political shift in the Kingdom of Vietnam. This coup reflected the ongoing power struggles within the Tran dynasty and set the stage for future conflicts.
events.name: Tran Ngung overthrows Tran Hien

events.enhanced_description: In 1388, Omar I was succeeded by Sa'id as the ruler of the Kanem-Bornu Empire, a significant political transition in the region. This change in leadership occurred amidst external pressures from Bilala invaders, highlighting the empire's vulnerabilities.
events.name: Omar I succeeded by Sa'id in Kanem-Bornu Empire

events.enhanced_description: In 1388, Ghiyas-ud-Din Tughluq II ascended to the throne as the Sultan of Delhi, succeeding Firuz Shah Tughlaq. His reign marked a continuation of the Tughlaq dynasty's influence over northern India during a period of political fragmentation.
events.name: Ghiyas-ud-Din Tughluq II succeeds Firuz Shah Tughlaq

events.enhanced_description: In 1388, Charles VI of France assumed full control of the government, effectively ending the regency of his uncle, Philip the Bold. This transition marked a significant moment in French history, as it set the stage for Charles's later struggles with mental illness and the ensuing political turmoil.
events.name: Charles VI of France takes control of the government

events.enhanced_description: In 1388, the University of Cologne was established, becoming one of the first universities in the Holy Roman Empire. By the 21st century, it would grow to be the largest university in Germany, playing a crucial role in the development of higher education in Europe.
events.name: The University of Cologne is established

events.enhanced_description: In 1388, the Cozia Monastery was constructed in Wallachia, serving as a significant religious and cultural site. This monastery reflects the architectural style of the time and has played an important role in the spiritual life of the region.
events.name: Cozia Monastery is built

events.enhanced_description: In 1388, the Ljubostinja Monastery was established in Serbia, becoming an important center for the Serbian Orthodox Church. The monastery is noted for its beautiful frescoes and architecture, reflecting the cultural heritage of the region.
events.name: Ljubostinja Monastery is built

events.enhanced_description: On April 9, 1388, the Battle of Näfels took place, where the forces of Glarus, allied with the Old Swiss Confederacy, decisively defeated the Habsburgs despite being heavily outnumbered. This battle was a significant victory for the Swiss and showcased their military prowess.
events.name: Battle of Näfels

events.enhanced_description: On May 18, 1388, the Battle of Buyur Lake occurred, where a Chinese Ming invasion force under General Lan Yu defeated a large Mongolian army led by Uskhal Khan Tögüs Temür. This battle marked a significant moment in the Ming Dynasty's efforts to consolidate power and eliminate Mongolian threats.
events.name: Battle of Buyur Lake

events.enhanced_description: On August 5, 1388, the Battle of Otterburn took place, where a Scottish army led by James Douglas defeated an English army, capturing their leader, Harry Hotspur. This battle was a significant event in the ongoing conflicts between Scotland and England.

image.caption: Medieval miniature depicting the Battle of Otterburn in Jean Froissart’s Chroniques.
image.credit: maître d'antoine de bourgogne et collab — BNF, fr. 2645, fol. 347r
image.date_qualification: Retrospective illustration created circa 1470–1475, depicting the 1388 battle; it is not contemporary to the event.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: Public domain; UsageTerms: Public domain; Copyrighted: False

events.name: Battle of Otterburn

events.enhanced_description: On August 27, 1388, the Battle of Bileća occurred, where Bosnian forces successfully checked the advance of the Ottomans. This battle was part of the broader struggle against Ottoman expansion in the Balkans.

locations.name: Bileća, Republika Srpska, Bosnia and Herzegovina

events.name: Battle of Bileća

events.enhanced_description: On December 12, 1388, Maria of Enghien sold the Lordship of Argos and Nauplia to the Republic of Venice. This transaction was part of Venice's strategic expansion in the region, enhancing its control over trade routes in the Aegean Sea.
events.name: Maria of Enghien sells the Lordship of Argos and Nauplia to the Republic of Venice

events.enhanced_description: In June 1389, the Käpplinge murders occurred in Stockholm, a politically motivated event that highlighted the tensions between the nobility and the monarchy in Sweden. This incident contributed to the ongoing power struggles within the kingdom.
events.name: Käpplinge murders in Stockholm

events.enhanced_description: In 1389, Bayezid I succeeded his father, Murad I, as the Sultan of the Ottoman Empire. His ascension marked the beginning of a new era characterized by aggressive expansion and consolidation of power within the empire.
events.name: Bayezid I succeeds Murad I

events.enhanced_description: In 1389, Stefan III succeeded his father as the ruler of Serbia, continuing the legacy of the Lazarević dynasty during a tumultuous period marked by external threats and internal strife.
events.name: Stefan III succeeds his father as ruler of Serbia

events.enhanced_description: In 1389, Mircea I of Wallachia and Polish King Władysław II Jagiełło signed a treaty aimed at mutual protection against Ottoman expansion. This alliance was crucial in the context of rising Ottoman power in Eastern Europe.
events.name: Mircea I and Władysław II Jagiełło sign treaty

events.enhanced_description: In 1389, the Goryeo Revolution culminated in the overthrow of King Chang, who was replaced by King Gongyang. This revolution was marked by internal strife and power struggles, leading to significant changes in the Goryeo dynasty.
events.name: Goryeo Revolution in Korea

events.enhanced_description: Hadji II was restored as the Mamluk Sultan of Egypt after successfully overthrowing Sultan Barquq. This event marked a significant power struggle within the Mamluk Sultanate, reflecting the turbulent political landscape of the time.
events.name: Hadji II is restored as Mamluk Sultan of Egypt

events.enhanced_description: With the backing of Antipope John XXIII, supporters of Louis II successfully overthrew the underage King Ladislaus of Naples. This political upheaval was recognized by Pope Boniface IX, further complicating the power dynamics in the region.
events.name: Supporters of Louis II overthrow King Ladislaus of Naples

events.enhanced_description: Wikramawardhana ascended to the throne as the ruler of the Majapahit Empire, succeeding Hayam Wuruk. This transition marked a significant moment in the history of one of Southeast Asia's most powerful empires.
events.name: Wikramawardhana succeeds Hayam Wuruk as ruler of the Majapahit Empire

events.enhanced_description: Sultan Tughluq Khan of Delhi was murdered, leading to the succession of his brother, Abu Bakr Shah. This event highlighted the instability and violence that characterized the politics of the Delhi Sultanate during this period.
events.name: Murder of Sultan Tughluq Khan of Delhi

events.enhanced_description: Biri II succeeded Kade Alunu as the King of the Kanem-Bornu Empire, which was located in present-day eastern Chad and Nigeria. This transition of power was significant for the empire's governance and territorial integrity.
events.name: Biri II succeeds Kade Alunu as King of the Kanem-Bornu Empire

events.enhanced_description: Sandaki overthrew Magha II to become the new Mansa of the Mali Empire. This change in leadership was pivotal for the empire, which was known for its wealth and cultural influence in West Africa.
events.name: Sandaki overthrows Magha II as Mansa of the Mali Empire

events.enhanced_description: Abd ar-Rahmân II succeeded Musa II as the ruler of the Ziyanid Dynasty in present-day western Algeria. This succession was part of the ongoing political dynamics within the region.
events.name: Abd ar-Rahmân II succeeds Musa II as ruler of the Ziyanid Dynasty

events.enhanced_description: Abu Tashufin II succeeded his nephew, Abu Hammu II, as the ruler of the Abdalwadid Dynasty in present-day eastern Algeria. This change in leadership was significant for the stability and governance of the dynasty.
events.name: Abu Tashufin II succeeds Abu Hammu II as ruler of the Abdalwadid Dynasty

events.enhanced_description: The Carmo Convent was constructed in Lisbon, Portugal, serving as a significant architectural and cultural landmark. Its establishment reflects the religious and artistic developments of the period.
events.name: Carmo Convent is built in Lisbon, Portugal

events.enhanced_description: On February 24, 1389, Queen Margaret of Norway and Denmark defeated Albert, King of Sweden, in a decisive battle, leading to her rule over all three kingdoms. This victory marked a significant consolidation of power in the Nordic region and the establishment of the Kalmar Union.
events.name: Queen Margaret defeats Albert of Sweden

events.enhanced_description: On May 3, 1389, Richard II of England regained control from the Lords Appellant, marking a pivotal moment in his reign. This shift restored royal authority and set the stage for Richard's later conflicts with the nobility.
events.name: Richard II takes control of England

events.enhanced_description: On May 19, 1389, Vasili I ascended to the position of Grand Prince of Moscow following the death of his father, Dmitry Donskoy. This transition marked the continuation of the Tatar-Mongol influence over Russia and the gradual rise of Moscow as a powerful state.

image.caption: Sakkos embroidery depicting Vasily I and Sofia Vitovtovna.
image.credit: anonimus — https://bigenc.ru/domestic_history/text/3795591
image.date_qualification: The image is dated between 1414 and 1417, 25–28 years after the accession event of 1389.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: CC BY-SA 4.0; UsageTerms: Creative Commons Attribution-Share Alike 4.0; Copyrighted: True

events.name: Vasili I becomes Grand Prince of Moscow

events.enhanced_description: On June 15, 1389, the Battle of Kosovo took place between the Ottoman Empire and Serbian forces, resulting in heavy casualties on both sides. The battle is notable for the deaths of Sultan Murad I and Serbian Prince Lazar, marking a significant moment in the struggle for control over the Balkans.
events.name: Battle of Kosovo

events.enhanced_description: On July 18, 1389, the kingdoms of England and France signed the Truce of Leulinghem, effectively ending the second phase of the Hundred Years' War. This agreement brought a temporary peace that lasted for 13 years, allowing both nations to regroup and reassess their strategies.
events.name: Truce of Leulinghem

events.enhanced_description: On November 2, 1389, Pope Boniface IX succeeded Pope Urban VI as the 203rd pope of the Roman Catholic Church. His papacy was marked by efforts to stabilize the Church during a period of schism and political turmoil.
events.name: Pope Boniface IX succeeds Pope Urban VI

events.enhanced_description: The Ottomans captured Philadelphia, marking the fall of the last significant Byzantine enclave in Anatolia. This event signified the gradual decline of Byzantine influence in the region.
events.name: Fall of Philadelphia to the Ottomans

events.enhanced_description: Barquq was restored as the Mamluk Sultan of Egypt after overthrowing Sultan Hadji II. This restoration was part of the ongoing power struggles within the Mamluk Sultanate.
events.name: Barquq is restored as Mamluk Sultan of Egypt

events.enhanced_description: Nasir ud din Muhammad Shah III overthrew his brother, Abu Bakr Shah, to become the Sultan of Delhi. This event was indicative of the intense familial rivalries that characterized the politics of the Delhi Sultanate.
figures: Nasir ud din Muhammad Shah III
events.name: Nasir ud din Muhammad Shah III overthrows Abu Bakr Shah as Sultan of Delhi

events.enhanced_description: Manuel III succeeded his father, Alexios III, as Emperor of Trebizond. His ascension marked a continuation of the imperial lineage in a region facing external pressures.
events.name: Manuel III succeeds Alexios III as Emperor of Trebizond

events.enhanced_description: Sikandar But-shikan succeeded Sikandar Shah as the Sultan of Kashmir. His reign would be marked by significant political and cultural developments in the region.
events.name: Sikandar But-shikan succeeds Sikandar Shah as Sultan of Kashmir

events.enhanced_description: Ko Cheng succeeded Che Bong Nga as the King of Champa, a significant event in the history of this ancient Southeast Asian civilization.

locations.name: Phan Rang-Tháp Chàm, Ninh Thuận, Vietnam

events.name: Ko Cheng succeeds Che Bong Nga as King of Champa

events.enhanced_description: Mahmud succeeded Sandaki as Mansa of the Mali Empire, restoring the Keita dynasty. This transition was crucial for the continuity of the empire's legacy and influence in West Africa.
events.name: Mahmud succeeds Sandaki as Mansa of the Mali Empire

events.enhanced_description: N'Diklam Sare succeeded Sare N'Dyaye as the ruler of the Jolof Empire, a significant event in the history of this West African kingdom.
events.name: N'Diklam Sare succeeds Sare N'Dyaye as ruler of the Jolof Empire

events.enhanced_description: The Kingdom of Kaffa was established in present-day Ethiopia, marking a significant development in the region's political landscape. This kingdom would play a crucial role in the history of Ethiopia.

locations.name: Kaffa Zone, Southern Nations, Nationalities, and Peoples' Region, Ethiopia
locations.region: Southern Nations, Nationalities, and Peoples' Region

events.name: Establishment of the Kingdom of Kaffa in present-day Ethiopia

events.enhanced_description: The Templo Mayor, the main temple of the Aztec capital Tenochtitlan, was constructed as a central place of worship dedicated to the gods Huitzilopochtli and Tlaloc. This monumental structure played a crucial role in the religious and cultural life of the Aztec civilization.
events.name: Templo Mayor built

events.enhanced_description: The Candi Surawana Temple was constructed during the height of the Majapahit Kingdom, reflecting the architectural and cultural achievements of the time. This temple is an important example of the Hindu-Buddhist influence in Indonesia.
events.name: Candi Surawana Temple built

events.enhanced_description: Construction of the San Petronio Basilica in Bologna began in 1390, intended to be the largest church in the world at the time. The basilica is notable for its unfinished façade and its significant role in the religious and cultural life of the city.
events.name: Construction begins on San Petronio Basilica

events.enhanced_description: In 1390, the Ottomans captured Philadelphia, marking the end of Byzantine control in the region. This event was part of the broader Ottoman expansion into Anatolia, significantly impacting the Byzantine Empire's presence in Asia Minor.
events.name: Ottomans take Philadelphia

events.enhanced_description: The Treaty of Lyck was signed, confirming an alliance between Vytautas and the Teutonic Knights during the Lithuanian Civil War against Vytautas's cousin, Jogaila. This treaty was crucial in shaping the political landscape of Eastern Europe.
events.name: Treaty of Lyck confirms alliance between Vytautas and the Teutonic Knights

events.enhanced_description: John VII Palaiologos successfully overthrew his grandfather, John V Palaiologos, to become the Byzantine Emperor. This power struggle illustrated the intense familial and political rivalries within the Byzantine court.
events.name: John VII Palaiologos overthrows John V Palaiologos as Byzantine Emperor

events.enhanced_description: Robert III succeeded his father, Robert II, as King of Scotland. This succession marked a continuation of the Stewart dynasty's rule over Scotland during a period of political challenges.
events.name: Robert III succeeds Robert II as King of Scotland

events.enhanced_description: The Treaty of Königsberg was signed during the Lithuanian Civil War between Samogitian nobles and representatives of the Teutonic Knights. This treaty aimed to solidify alliances and resolve conflicts in the region.
events.name: Treaty of Königsberg signed in Lithuanian Civil War

events.enhanced_description: The coalition of Vytautas and the Teutonic Knights began a five-week siege of Vilnius during the Lithuanian Civil War. Notably, the Duke of Hereford, who would later become King Henry IV of England, participated in this military campaign.
events.name: Siege of Vilnius begins during Lithuanian Civil War

events.enhanced_description: After John V Palaiologos was restored by his son Manuel and the Republic of Venice, John VII Palaiologos sought refuge with the Ottoman Sultan Bayezid I. This event underscores the complex relationships between the Byzantine Empire and the rising Ottoman power.
events.name: John VII Palaiologos seeks refuge with Ottoman Sultan Bayezid I

events.enhanced_description: Henry III succeeded his father, John I, as King of Castile and León. His reign would be marked by efforts to consolidate power and navigate the complex political landscape of late medieval Spain.
events.name: Henry III succeeds John I as King of Castile and León

events.enhanced_description: In 1391, Manuel II Palaiologos ascended to the Byzantine throne following the death of his father, John V Palaiologos. His reign would be marked by the decline of the Byzantine Empire and increasing pressure from the Ottoman Turks.

image.caption: Portrait of Byzantine emperor Manuel II Palaiologos.
image.credit: The original uploader was Pitchka — File:Manuel_II_Paleologus.jpg
image.date_qualification: The supplied image date is 2021-02-26; it is not a date for the depicted portrait or the 1391 accession.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: CC BY-SA 4.0; UsageTerms: Creative Commons Attribution-Share Alike 4.0; Copyrighted: True

events.name: Manuel II Palaiologos becomes Byzantine emperor

events.enhanced_description: Yusuf II succeeded Muhammed V as the Nasrid Sultan of Granada in 1391, during a tumultuous period for the Nasrid dynasty. His reign would face challenges from both internal factions and external pressures from the Christian kingdoms of Spain.
events.name: Yusuf II succeeds Muhammed V

events.enhanced_description: Stephen Dabiša succeeded Stephen Tvrtko I as the King of Bosnia in 1391, during a period marked by political instability and territorial disputes. His reign would be characterized by efforts to consolidate power amidst external threats.
events.name: Stephen Dabiša succeeds Stephen Tvrtko I

events.enhanced_description: Shah Mansur ascended to leadership of the Timurid-occupied Muzaffarid Empire in 1391, navigating the complexities of regional politics and the influence of the Timurids. His rule was marked by efforts to maintain autonomy amid external pressures.
events.name: Shah Mansur becomes leader of the Muzaffarid Empire

events.enhanced_description: In 1391, Zafar Khan Muzaffar led a group of Muzaffarids to establish a new Sultanate in Gujarat, marking a significant development in the region's political landscape. This Sultanate would play a key role in the history of Gujarat and the surrounding areas.
events.name: Muzaffarids establish Sultanate at Gujarat

events.enhanced_description: In 1391, Vytautas the Great, a prominent figure in Lithuanian history, formed a strategic alliance with Muscovy to strengthen his position against external threats. This alliance was crucial for the political dynamics of Eastern Europe during this period.
events.name: Vytautas the Great forms alliance with Muscovy

events.enhanced_description: Roman I succeeded Petru as the Prince of Moldavia in 1391, during a time of political fragmentation and external pressures from neighboring powers. His reign would be marked by efforts to stabilize and strengthen the principality.
events.name: Roman I succeeds Petru as Prince of Moldavia

events.enhanced_description: In 1391, Konrad von Wallenrode succeeded Konrad Zöllner von Rotenstein as the Grand Master of the Teutonic Knights, a position that held significant influence in the Baltic region. His leadership would be pivotal in the Order's military and political endeavors.
events.name: Konrad von Wallenrode succeeds as Grand Master of the Teutonic Knights

events.enhanced_description: In 1391, Bridget of Sweden was canonized by Pope Boniface IX, recognizing her contributions to the Catholic Church and her role as a mystic and founder of the Bridgettine order. Her canonization marked an important moment in the history of saints in the Church.
events.name: Bridget of Sweden canonized by Pope Boniface IX

events.enhanced_description: In 1391, Ushkuinik pirates from Novgorod launched attacks on the Muscovy towns of Zhukotin and Kazan, highlighting the ongoing conflicts and instability in the region. These raids were part of the broader maritime piracy that affected trade and security in the area.
events.name: Ushkuinik pirates sack Muscovy towns

events.enhanced_description: In 1391, the Chinese invented toilet paper, initially used by emperors, marking a significant advancement in hygiene and personal care. This innovation would eventually spread and become a common household item worldwide.
events.name: Invention of toilet paper in China

events.enhanced_description: In 1391, Henry I Sinclair, Earl of Orkney, asserted control over the Shetland Islands and the Faroe Islands, expanding his influence in the North Atlantic. This move was part of the broader Norse exploration and settlement patterns in the region.
events.name: Henry I Sinclair takes control of Shetland and Faroe Islands

events.enhanced_description: The University of Ferrara was founded in 1391, becoming one of the first universities in Italy. It played a significant role in the development of higher education and the intellectual life of the region.
events.name: University of Ferrara founded

events.enhanced_description: In 1391, the Ming government ordered the planting of 50 million trees in the Nanjing area, reflecting an early recognition of environmental conservation and the importance of forestry for ecological balance. This initiative aimed to combat deforestation and promote sustainable practices.
events.name: Ming government orders tree planting

events.enhanced_description: The Massacre of 1391 was a series of anti-Jewish pogroms that erupted in Seville, leading to the deaths of thousands of Jews and forcing many survivors to convert to Christianity or flee. This event marked a significant turning point in the history of Jews in Spain.
events.name: Massacre of 1391

events.enhanced_description: The Battle of the Kondurcha River in 1391 saw Timur decisively defeat Tokhtamysh of the Golden Horde, solidifying Timur's power and influence in Central Asia. This battle was part of the larger conflict between the two leaders for dominance in the region.
events.name: Battle of the Kondurcha River

events.enhanced_description: In 1392, King Jogaila of Poland and Lithuania appointed his cousin Vytautas the Great as regent of Lithuania, a strategic move to stabilize the region. In exchange, Vytautas relinquished his claim to the Lithuanian throne, replacing Jogaila's unpopular brother Skirgaila as regent, which marked a significant shift in power dynamics within the Grand Duchy.
events.name: Appointment of Vytautas the Great as Regent of Lithuania

events.enhanced_description: In 1392, Muhammed VII ascended to the throne as the Nasrid Sultan of Granada, succeeding his father Yusuf II. His reign occurred during a tumultuous period marked by internal strife and the looming threat of the Christian Reconquista.
events.name: Muhammed VII succeeds Yusuf II as Sultan of Granada

events.enhanced_description: In 1392, Franciscan friar James of Jülich was executed by boiling for impersonating a bishop and unlawfully ordaining priests. This event highlighted the tensions within the Church and the severe consequences of clerical misconduct during the medieval period.
events.name: Execution of James of Jülich

events.enhanced_description: In 1392, Maria, Queen of Sicily, successfully defeated an army of rebel barons, consolidating her power and authority in the region. This victory was crucial in maintaining the stability of her reign amidst the challenges posed by noble dissent.
events.name: Maria, Queen of Sicily defeats rebel barons

events.enhanced_description: In 1392, William le Scrope succeeded William II de Montacute as King of Mann. His ascension marked a continuation of the complex feudal allegiances and political maneuvering characteristic of the Isle of Man during this period.
events.name: William le Scrope becomes King of Mann

events.enhanced_description: In 1392, Seoan mac Pilib succeeded Tomas mor mac Mathghamhna as King of East Breifne, a region in north-central Ireland. His reign was part of the ongoing struggles for power among Gaelic lords during a time of significant political fragmentation.
events.name: Seoan mac Pilib becomes King of East Breifne

events.enhanced_description: In 1392, Sultan Beyazid I of the Ottoman Empire conquered the city of Afyonkarahisar, a strategic location in western Anatolia. This conquest was part of Beyazid's broader campaign to expand Ottoman territory and influence in the region.
events.name: Conquest of Afyonkarahisar by Sultan Beyazid I

events.enhanced_description: In 1392, Louis de Valois was created the first Duke of Orléans of the second creation, a title that would carry significant political weight in the French nobility. This event underscored the importance of noble titles in the power dynamics of medieval France.
events.name: Creation of Duke of Orléans

events.enhanced_description: In 1392, Erfurt University was founded in Erfurt, becoming one of the earliest universities in Germany. This institution played a crucial role in the development of higher education in the region and contributed to the intellectual life of the late medieval period.
events.name: Foundation of Erfurt University

events.enhanced_description: In 1392, Penistone Grammar School was founded near Barnsley, England. This institution would later become one of the first community comprehensive schools in England, reflecting the evolving landscape of education during the medieval period.
events.name: Foundation of Penistone Grammar School

events.enhanced_description: On June 13, 1392, an assassination attempt by Pierre de Craon against Olivier de Clisson, the Constable of France, failed, highlighting the intense political rivalries and conflicts during the Hundred Years' War. This incident underscored the precarious nature of power in late medieval France.
events.name: Assassination attempt against Olivier de Clisson

events.enhanced_description: On August 5, 1392, General Yi Sŏng-gye crowned himself Taejo of Joseon, marking the end of the Goryeo dynasty and the establishment of the Joseon dynasty, which would last over five centuries. This transition was pivotal in shaping Korean history and culture.
events.name: General Yi Sŏng-gye crowns himself Taejo of Joseon

events.enhanced_description: On December 16, 1392, Emperor Go-Kameyama of Japan abdicated in favor of rival claimant Go-Komatsu, effectively ending the nanboku-cho period of conflict between the Northern and Southern imperial courts. This event was significant in restoring stability to the Japanese imperial lineage.
events.name: Emperor Go-Kameyama abdicates

events.enhanced_description: In 1393, the Muzaffarid Empire, led by Shah Mansur, rebelled against their Timurid occupiers in central Persia. The rebellion was ultimately crushed, leading to the execution of the Muzaffarid nobility and the end of their dynasty.
events.name: Muzaffarid Rebellion against Timurids

events.enhanced_description: In 1393, George VII succeeded his father, Bagrat V, as King of Georgia. His reign continued the legacy of his father's rule during a time of political instability and external threats.
events.name: George VII becomes King of Georgia

events.enhanced_description: In 1393, Abdul Aziz II ascended to the throne of the Marinid dynasty in present-day Morocco following the death of Sultan Abu Al-Abbas. His reign was marked by the challenges of maintaining control over a fragmented kingdom.
events.name: Abdul Aziz II becomes Sultan of the Marinid dynasty

events.enhanced_description: In 1393, Raimondo Del Balzo Orsini succeeded Otto, Duke of Brunswick-Grubenhagen, as Prince of Taranto in southeastern Italy. His rule was part of the complex feudal landscape of the Italian peninsula during this period.
events.name: Raimondo Del Balzo Orsini becomes Prince of Taranto

events.enhanced_description: In 1393, Samsenethai succeeded his father, Fa Ngum, as King of Lan Xang, a kingdom in present-day Laos. His reign continued the legacy of his father's efforts to consolidate power and expand the kingdom's influence.
events.name: Samsenethai becomes King of Lan Xang

events.enhanced_description: In 1393, James I of Cyprus inherited the title of King of Armenia after the death of his distant cousin Leo VI. Despite this title, the Mamluk conquerors from Egypt remained the true rulers of the region.
events.name: James I of Cyprus inherits title of King of Armenia

events.enhanced_description: In 1393, a record from the Ming dynasty noted the production of 720,000 sheets of toilet paper for the imperial court in Beijing, showcasing the sophistication of Chinese manufacturing and the importance of hygiene in court life.
events.name: Ming dynasty toilet paper production record

events.enhanced_description: In 1393, Bosnia mounted a resistance against an invasion by the Ottoman Empire, reflecting the growing tensions between the Ottomans and the Balkan states. This resistance was part of the larger struggle for autonomy and control in the region.
events.name: Bosnia resists Ottoman invasion

events.enhanced_description: In 1393, the Ottoman Turks captured Turnovgrad, the capital city of eastern Bulgaria, allowing Emperor Ivan Shishman to remain as a puppet ruler. This event marked a significant step in the Ottoman expansion into the Balkans.
events.name: Capture of Turnovgrad by Ottoman Turks

events.enhanced_description: In 1393, despite a treaty with the king of Poland, Roman I of Moldavia supported Fyodor Koriatovych against the king. This decision led to his defeat in battle and the subsequent loss of his throne the following year.
events.name: Roman I of Moldavia supports Fyodor Koriatovych

events.enhanced_description: In 1393, Sikander Shah I succeeded Muhammad Shah III as Sultan of Delhi. His brief reign was marked by political instability and challenges from rival factions within the sultanate.
events.name: Sikander Shah I becomes Sultan of Delhi

events.enhanced_description: In 1393, Abu Thabid II succeeded Abu Tashufin II as ruler of the Abdalwadid dynasty in present-day eastern Algeria. His rule was characterized by internal strife and the challenges of maintaining control over a fragmented territory.
events.name: Abu Thabid II becomes ruler of the Abdalwadid dynasty

events.enhanced_description: In 1393, Konrad von Jungingen succeeded Konrad von Wallenrode as Grand Master of the Teutonic Knights. His leadership would influence the Order's military and political strategies in the Baltic region.
events.name: Konrad von Jungingen becomes Grand Master of the Teutonic Knights

events.enhanced_description: In 1393, Maelruanaidh MacDermot ascended to the throne of Magh Luirg, a territory in north-central Ireland, succeeding Aedh MacDermot. This transition marked a significant moment in the local Gaelic lordship dynamics during a period of political fragmentation in Ireland.
events.name: Maelruanaidh MacDermot succeeds Aedh MacDermot, as King of Magh Luirg in north-central Ireland

events.enhanced_description: In 1393, King Stjepan Dabiša of Bosnia signed the Contract of Djakovice with King Sigismund of Hungary, which established a crucial peace agreement between the two kingdoms. This treaty was significant in stabilizing relations in the region during a time of political turbulence.
events.name: King Stjepan Dabiša of Bosnia signs the Contract of Djakovice, establishing peace with King Sigismund of Hungary

events.enhanced_description: In 1393, the Byzantine Empire lost control of Thessaly to the expanding Ottoman Empire, marking a significant territorial loss. This event was part of the Ottomans' broader campaign to consolidate power in the Balkans.
events.name: Byzantium loses Thessaly to the growing Ottoman Empire

events.enhanced_description: On January 28, 1393, the Bal des Ardents took place in Paris, where four members of the court of Charles VI tragically died in a fire during a masquerade ball. This event highlighted the dangers of courtly celebrations and the precarious nature of royal life.
events.name: Bal des Ardents

events.enhanced_description: On March 23, 1393, John of Nepomuk, a Bohemian priest, was killed in Prague by being thrown off Charles Bridge into the Vltava River, allegedly at the behest of King Wenceslaus IV. His martyrdom would later lead to his canonization as a saint.
events.name: Death of John of Nepomuk

events.enhanced_description: In 1394, the Ottomans conquered Thessaly and initiated an eight-year siege of Constantinople, marking a critical phase in their campaign against the Byzantine Empire. This siege would ultimately lead to the fall of Constantinople in 1453.
events.name: The Ottomans conquer Thessaly and begin an eight-year siege of Constantinople

events.enhanced_description: In 1394, Ashikaga Yoshimitsu retired as shōgun of Japan, passing the title to his son, Ashikaga Yoshimochi. This transition marked a significant moment in the Ashikaga shogunate, influencing the political landscape of Japan.

image.caption: Ashikaga Yoshimitsu’s kaō (signature), reproduced from a 1690 source.
image.credit: 丸山可澄 — 花押藪 , image. 50.
image.date_qualification: The image date is 1690, not the 1394 event date.
