events.name: Eric of Pomerania is deposed from the Swedish throne

events.enhanced_description: In February 1436, Charles Knutsson was appointed as joint rikshövitsman alongside Engelbrekt Engelbrektsson, marking a significant shift in leadership during a turbulent period in Swedish history. The two leaders would collaborate until Engelbrekt's untimely death.
events.name: Charles Knutsson becomes joint rikshövitsman

events.enhanced_description: In April 1436, during the Hundred Years' War, French forces successfully recaptured Paris from English occupation. This pivotal victory was a significant turning point in the conflict, bolstering French morale and asserting their control over the capital.
events.name: Paris is recaptured from the English

events.enhanced_description: On May 4, 1436, Engelbrekt Engelbrektsson was murdered while en route to Stockholm for negotiations, leading to a power vacuum in Swedish leadership. Following his death, Charles Knutsson temporarily assumed control, and the first meeting of the Riksdag of the Estates is believed to have occurred in Uppsala shortly thereafter.
events.name: Murder of Engelbrekt Engelbrektsson

events.enhanced_description: On June 25, 1436, Scottish princess Margaret Stewart married Louis XI of France in Tours. This union was politically significant, strengthening ties between Scotland and France during a period of conflict with England.
events.name: Margaret Stewart marries Louis XI of France

events.enhanced_description: On July 5, 1436, the Hussite Wars effectively came to an end in Bohemia, with Sigismund being accepted as King. This resolution marked a significant moment in Czech history, concluding years of religious and political conflict.
events.name: End of the Hussite Wars

events.enhanced_description: On July 29, 1436, French forces abandoned their long-standing Siege of Calais, a strategic port city that had been a focal point in the Hundred Years' War. This retreat reflected the challenges faced by the French military during this protracted conflict.
events.name: Siege of Calais abandoned

events.enhanced_description: On August 30, 1436, Brunelleschi's Dome at Florence Cathedral was dedicated, showcasing the architectural innovation of the Renaissance. This dome remains a masterpiece of engineering and design, symbolizing the artistic achievements of the period.
events.name: Dedication of Brunelleschi's Dome

events.enhanced_description: On September 1, 1436, Eric of Pomerania was reinstated as king of Sweden, marking a turbulent return to power. Concurrently, Charles Knutsson resigned from his position as rikshövitsman, reflecting the ongoing political instability in the region.
events.name: Eric of Pomerania reinstated as king of Sweden

events.enhanced_description: On September 10, 1436, the Battle of Piperdean took place, where Scottish forces achieved a decisive victory over the English. This battle was part of the ongoing conflicts between Scotland and England during the period.

image.caption: Photograph of Piperdean, near Old Cambus in the Scottish Borders.
image.credit: Richard Webb — From geograph.org.uk
image.date_qualification: Photographed 6 April 2006; the article excerpt dates the battle to 10 September 1435.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: CC BY-SA 2.0; UsageTerms: Creative Commons Attribution-Share Alike 2.0; Copyrighted: True

events.name: Battle of Piperdean

events.enhanced_description: In June 1437, a peasant army gathered at Bobâlna, marking the beginning of the Transylvanian peasant revolt against the feudal lords. This revolt was ultimately suppressed by January of the following year.
events.name: Transylvanian peasant revolt gathering at Bobâlna

events.enhanced_description: In 1437, the Sandside Chase took place in Caithness, where Clan Mackay defeated Clan Gunn. This conflict was part of the ongoing clan rivalries that characterized Scottish history during this period.
events.name: Sandside Chase

events.enhanced_description: The Kazan Khanate was established in 1437, becoming a significant political entity in the region. It played a crucial role in the history of Tatar and Russian interactions.
events.name: Establishment of the Kazan Khanate

events.enhanced_description: In 1437, Ulugh Beg published the Zij-i Sultani, a comprehensive star catalogue that significantly advanced the field of astronomy. This work is considered one of the most important astronomical texts of the medieval Islamic world.
events.name: Publication of Ulugh Beg's Zij-i Sultani star catalogue

events.enhanced_description: On February 20, 1437, James I of Scotland was fatally stabbed at Perth during a failed coup orchestrated by his uncle, Walter Stewart, Earl of Atholl. This assassination plunged Scotland into further political instability and conflict.
events.name: James I of Scotland is fatally stabbed

events.enhanced_description: On March 11, 1437, Nova Scorpii was observed from Seoul, Korea, marking a significant astronomical event. This observation contributed to the understanding of celestial phenomena in East Asia.
events.name: Nova Scorpii AD 1437 observed from Seoul

events.enhanced_description: On March 25, 1437, James II of Scotland was crowned at Holyrood Abbey at the tender age of six by Pope Eugene IV. This event marked a significant moment in Scottish history, as the capital was moved to Edinburgh for the security of the crown.
events.name: James II of Scotland crowned

events.enhanced_description: On April 23, 1437, the city of Malmö, which was then part of Denmark, officially received its current coat of arms. This heraldic symbol has since become a significant representation of the city's identity.
events.name: Malmö receives its current coat of arms

events.enhanced_description: On October 19, 1437, a Portuguese military expedition aimed at conquering Tangier ended in failure, resulting in the capture of Prince Ferdinand as a hostage. This event highlighted the challenges faced by Portugal in its early attempts at expansion in North Africa.
events.name: Portuguese attempt to conquer Tangier fails

events.enhanced_description: On December 9, 1437, Sigismund, Holy Roman Emperor, passed away in Zagreb. His death marked a significant transition in European politics as he was succeeded by Frederick III, altering the balance of power in the region.
events.name: Death of Sigismund, Holy Roman Emperor

events.enhanced_description: In 1438, Albert II of Habsburg ascended to the throne as King of Hungary, marking a significant moment in the Habsburg dynasty's influence in Central Europe.

image.caption: Detail from the Albrecht Altar at Klosterneuburg Abbey depicting King Albrecht II.
image.credit: Unknown author Unknown author — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:304K%C3%B6nig_Albrecht_II.jpg
image.date_qualification: Portrait detail, not a record of the coronation; image date is circa 1438.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: Public domain; UsageTerms: Public domain; Copyrighted: False

events.name: Albert II of Habsburg becomes King of Hungary

events.enhanced_description: In October 1438, Eric of Pomerania lost direct control of Sweden when Karl Knutsson Bonde was elected as Regent. This marked a significant shift in the governance of Sweden during the Kalmar Union.
events.name: Loss of control of Sweden by Eric of Pomerania

events.enhanced_description: The siege of Brescia, initiated on July 11, 1438, was raised after the arrival of Scaramuccia da Forlì, who intervened against the condottieri troops of Niccolò Piccinino. This event underscored the volatile nature of Italian city-state politics.
events.name: Siege of Brescia raised

events.enhanced_description: In 1438, Pachacuti ascended to power in the Kingdom of Cusco, initiating a period of expansion that would lead to the establishment of the Inca Empire, known as Tahuantinsuyu.
events.name: Pachacuti becomes ruler of the Kingdom of Cusco

events.enhanced_description: In 1438, Nang Keo Phimpha briefly became queen of Lan Xang before being deposed and killed. Her short reign reflects the turbulent political landscape of the region during this period.
events.name: Nang Keo Phimpha becomes queen of Lan Xang

events.enhanced_description: In 1438, the Ming dynasty court decided to close all silver mines and prohibit private silver mining in the provinces of Zhejiang and Fujian. This drastic measure aimed to control the influx of silver into the economy, reflecting the complexities of Ming economic policies.
events.name: Ming dynasty silver mining prohibition

events.enhanced_description: In 1438, the Sukhothai Kingdom merged with the Ayutthaya Kingdom, leading to the consolidation of power in the region and the eventual rise of the Ayutthaya Kingdom as a dominant force in Southeast Asia.
events.name: Merger of Sukhothai and Ayutthaya Kingdoms

events.enhanced_description: On January 9, 1438, the city of Cluj (Kolozsvár) was conquered, effectively ending the Transylvanian peasant revolt that had begun in Bobâlna. This marked a significant defeat for the peasant forces.
events.name: Conquest of Cluj marks end of Transylvanian peasant revolt

events.enhanced_description: The Council of Florence opened on January 10, 1438, in Ferrara, aiming to address issues within the Catholic Church and promote unity among Christian denominations.
events.name: Opening of the Council of Florence

events.enhanced_description: On February 2, 1438, the Unio Trium Nationum pact was established in Transylvania, which aimed to create a political alliance among the three nations of Transylvania: the Hungarians, the Saxons, and the Szeklers.
events.name: Establishment of the Unio Trium Nationum pact

events.enhanced_description: On February 10, 1438, All Souls' College was founded at the University of Oxford by Henry Chichele, Archbishop of Canterbury, and King Henry VI of England, establishing a significant institution for graduate studies.
events.name: Founding of All Souls' College, Oxford

events.enhanced_description: On March 18, 1438, Albert II of Habsburg was crowned King of Germany, further solidifying the Habsburg influence in Central Europe during a time of political fragmentation.
events.name: Albert II of Habsburg becomes King of Germany

events.enhanced_description: On April 14, 1438, the County of Holland declared war on several cities of the Hanseatic League, initiating the Dutch–Hanseatic War. This conflict arose from trade disputes and territorial ambitions.
events.name: Dutch–Hanseatic War declaration

events.enhanced_description: On July 7, 1438, Charles VII of France issued the Pragmatic Sanction of Bourges, which granted the French church control over the appointment of bishops, significantly reducing papal influence in France.
events.name: Pragmatic Sanction of Bourges issued

events.enhanced_description: On September 13, 1438, Afonso V ascended to the throne as King of Portugal, beginning a reign that would see significant territorial expansion and the strengthening of the Portuguese crown.
events.name: Afonso V becomes King of Portugal

events.enhanced_description: Around 1439, Johannes Gutenberg developed the technology of printing with movable type in Mainz, Germany. This revolutionary invention greatly facilitated the spread of knowledge and literature, marking the beginning of the Printing Revolution and significantly impacting the course of European history.
events.name: Johannes Gutenberg develops printing with movable type

events.enhanced_description: In 1439, the French Estates-General adopted the Great Ordinance, which granted the king exclusive rights to raise troops and established the taille, a taxation measure to support a standing army. This ordinance was a significant step in centralizing royal power in France.
events.name: The Great Ordinance is adopted by the French Estates-General

events.enhanced_description: In 1439, the Council of Florence was relocated to Florence, Italy, where it aimed to address issues of church reform and the reconciliation of the Eastern and Western churches. This council was pivotal in the efforts to resolve the East-West Schism.
events.name: The Council of Florence is moved to Florence

events.enhanced_description: In 1439, during the Portuguese Cortes, Peter, Duke of Coimbra, was appointed as the Regent of the Kingdom of Portugal. His appointment was significant in the political landscape of Portugal during a time of internal strife and external threats.
events.name: Peter, Duke of Coimbra is appointed Regent of the Kingdom

events.enhanced_description: On May 4, 1439, the Battle of Grotnik occurred, where Władysław III's royal army defeated the Hussite forces in Poland. This battle was part of the larger conflict involving the Hussite movement.
events.name: Battle of Grotnik

events.enhanced_description: On June 29, 1439, the date of the Miracle of the Moose, attributed to Venerable Macarius, is commemorated according to Russian hagiographers. This event highlights the significance of saints in Russian Orthodox tradition.
events.name: Miracle of the Moose

events.enhanced_description: On July 6, 1439, Pope Eugene IV issued the Bull of Union with the Greeks during the Council of Florence, aiming to reconcile the Eastern Orthodox Church with the Roman Catholic Church and proclaiming the end of the East-West Schism. However, this effort was largely rejected by the Eastern bishops shortly thereafter, reflecting the deep divisions that persisted between the two branches of Christianity.
events.name: Pope Eugene IV issues the Bull of Union with the Greeks

events.enhanced_description: On September 8, 1439, Cardinal Giovanni Vitelleschi captured the city of Foligno, effectively ending the Trinci family's rule over the region. This event marked a significant shift in power dynamics within the Papal States during a period of political turmoil.
events.name: Cardinal Giovanni Vitelleschi captures Foligno

events.enhanced_description: On September 29, 1439, Eric of Pomerania, the King of Sweden, Denmark, and Norway, was declared deposed in Sweden, leading to Karl Knutsson Bonde continuing his role as Regent. This event was pivotal in the political landscape of the Kalmar Union, which sought to unify the three kingdoms under a single monarch.

image.caption: Statue of Eric the Pomeranian at Darłowo Castle, Poland.
